observations.source_locator: Results > Blood gas values and Oxygen transfer performance; operating-point results
limitations: The source reports 39.095 mL O2/L blood; blood-gas samples were taken before and after the oxygenator and sampled again after 6 minutes, with measured values averaged for transfer calculation.
Only one feasibility test was performed and no statistical analysis was conducted; sample size, repeatability and run-level variance are not established.
The test used abattoir porcine blood under ISO 7199 conditioning, not human fetal blood or a developing subject.
The paper states that its oxygen-transfer measurements did not reach the reported 24- and 28-week fetal-age targets; those requirements are not treatment settings or proof of clinical adequacy.
Data are available from the corresponding author on request, but no request was made; the public article route does not expose machine-readable run-level values.

measurement_conditions.source_locator: Methods > Experimental setup; pressure measured in dual-compartment mode

limitations: Only one in-vitro feasibility test was performed and no statistical analysis was conducted.
The test used abattoir porcine blood under ISO 7199 conditioning, not human fetal blood or a developing subject.
The paper-defined 20 mmHg pressure-drop criterion is an engineering design target, not a clinical threshold.

The Results text gives the 45.4 mmHg pressure-loss value at “190 mmHg,” while Methods and the Figure 5 caption describe the pressure sweep by blood flow from 50 to 190 mL/min; that condition-unit mismatch is preserved as unresolved in the source inventory.
Raw data are available from the corresponding author on request, but no request was made and no author was contacted.
